newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU refers STN Atlas buy to German cartel office.
newsitem.headline: EU refers STN Atlas buy to German cartel office.

text.p: German defence group Rheinmetall AG said on Thursday that European Commission competition regulators had referred the military aspects of its takeover of STN Atlas to Germany's cartel office.

Rheinmetall, together with German utility Badenwerk AG, last December signed a contract to buy 51 percent of electronics company STN Atlas. British Aerospace Plc signed up to buy the remaining 49 percent.
Rheinmetall said in a statement issued to Reuters that the referral had been expected, and the cartel authority would only review the implications of the takeover on the market for armoured vehicles.
The takeover of STN's other areas -- simulators, marine and ship technology and other systems -- did not raise regulatory questions and would not be reviewed by the Berlin-based office.
Rheinmetall also said a "concrete industrial solution" was crystallising which would integrate its two main competitors in the armoured vehicles business -- Krauss Maffei and Wegmann.
"With that the approval process for STN Atlas Elektronik can be positively concluded and the business' future secured," Rheinmetall said.

The Rheinmetall group's military arm makes the Panzerhaubitze 2000 mobile artillery gun, to be delivered next year to the German army, the Keiler landmine clearer and the lightweight Wiesel armoured car.

STN Atlas was sold off last year by the liquidators of bankrupt north German shipyard group Bremer Vulkan AG after a long tender process in which the Defence Ministry intervened to prevent the company being sold abroad completely.
The total sale price was 550 million marks ($320 million).
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.716 German Marks)
